summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 of the cipher-box project, migrating the TEE worker to Phala Cloud CVM with full monorepo integration, tests, instrumentation, and deployment verification.
summary.outcome: All 6 plans completed across 4 waves: TEE worker relocated to apps/tee-worker/ with shared packages, 58 unit tests added, Phala SDK integrated with Prometheus metrics, staging CI/CD updated, and CVM deployed and verified on Phala Cloud production infrastructure. PR #395 created with security fixes, lint fixes, and all review comments resolved.

repo: Phala Cloud has no separate testnet — the free tier runs on production nodes (Intel TDX, dstack-pha-prod5). Phase 35 was named 'phala-testnet' but the CVM runs on production Phala infrastructure.
The `entire` branch stores full conversation transcripts as JSONL files and is pushed automatically — any credentials shared in conversation will be checkpointed to this branch.
HANDOFF.json and .continue-here.md are used for cross-session/cross-machine resumption; they should never contain live credentials.

The staging deploy workflow (deploy-staging.yml) has build-tee and deploy-tee-phala jobs that auto-deploy the CVM when a staging-v* tag is pushed, using PHALA_CLOUD_API_KEY and STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET from GitHub staging environment secrets.
TEE_WORKER_SECRET must be kept in sync between the API's staging .env on the VPS and the Phala CVM deployment — both are injected from the same GitHub staging secret.
multiformats package (providing CID.parse) is a dependency of @cipherbox/crypto and should be used for CID validation rather than hand-rolled regex.
undici is bundled with Node.js but requires explicit installation as a dev dependency for TypeScript types in pnpm workspaces.

code.finding: Original implementation called getKeypair() instead of getPublicKey(), leaking private key material into the route scope.

DNS pinning via hostname rewrite (changing URL host to resolved IP) breaks TLS SNI and certificate validation. Correct approach: use undici Agent with a custom lookup function so the original hostname is preserved for TLS while the connection goes to the pinned IP.
SSRF bypass check compared endpoint variable against 'cipherbox' instead of the protocol variable — a logic bug that would allow non-cipherbox protocols to bypass the check.
parseInt(process.env.TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH || '1', 10) yields NaN if the env var is set to a non-numeric string. Fixed with explicit isFinite check and fallback to 1.
Buffer.from(hex, 'hex') silently truncates invalid hex chars. Explicit validation of hex string format (non-empty, even length, /^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/) should precede unwrapKey call.
404/unmatched route label should be '/:unmatched' not 'unmatched' to align with the API's http-metrics.interceptor.ts pattern and prevent unbounded Prometheus label cardinality.
FetchFn type was exported from types.ts but not re-exported from the pinning barrel index, forcing consumers to use ProviderOptions['fetchFn'] or deep-import.

workflow: GSD pause-work/resume-work successfully transferred execution context across machines (development machine → Docker host → back). HANDOFF.json provides structured machine-readable state; .continue-here.md provides human context.
When parallel executor agents commit with --no-verify, worktree merge conflicts in STATE.md and ROADMAP.md are common and require manual resolution taking the agent's version.
Git worktree-based parallel agent execution can hit git config lock contention; sequential execution of Wave 2 agents resolved the issue.
Security review should be done before creating a PR, not after — several high/medium findings required post-PR commits.
Credentials pasted into Claude conversations appear in the entire/ branch transcripts automatically. Rotate any secrets shared in conversation regardless of whether they appear in committed files.

friction: Usage limit interruption mid-Wave 2 parallel execution — both agents failed and required manual retry sequentially
Git config lock contention prevented parallel worktree agent execution for Wave 2; had to fall back to sequential
Worktree merge was complicated by STATE.md conflicts on every wave merge — required manual resolution each time
gsd-tools init failed when run from the main repo instead of the worktree, requiring discovery of the correct working directory
undici TypeScript types not auto-resolved in pnpm workspace despite being bundled with Node.js — required explicit pnpm add undici
Phala CLI restart command doesn't provide a clean wait mechanism — required polling with curl retries and significant wait times
Handoff files (HANDOFF.json, .continue-here.md) included live credentials that were pushed to remote and later appeared in entire/ branch transcripts, requiring credential rotation
open_items: SSRF connection-test.ts vs sdk-core probe deduplication — significant refactor deferred from /simplify review

Phala CVM deployment currently requires manual staging tag push to redeploy with rotated credentials — the old (now-revoked) API key and TEE worker secret are in git history on the phase-35 branch and entire/ transcript
The 35-HUMAN-UAT.md file persists with status: partial and will surface in future /gsd:progress and /gsd:audit-uat until explicitly verified/closed
Phase 35 directory is named 'phala-testnet-tee-migration' which is a misnomer — docs updated but directory name retained to avoid breaking cross-references
Republish latency baselines (~1155ms avg) are network-bound from the test machine to Phala Cloud prod5 — production co-located latency not yet measured
CVM epoch persistence tested only through one restart cycle — long-term epoch stability under production load not validated
